clue.text: Playing of requiems interrupted by a very short note

indicators.note: playing music means performing it, and here the letters are performed in a fresh arrangement
to interrupt is to break into the middle, so one piece is pushed inside another

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
taken as written
V is the standard abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: A performance of requiems is broken up by a brief musical note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very short note' looks like the definition, but 'very' supplies V; rearrange REQUIEMS to SEMIQU-ER and drop A V into the middle to get SEMIQUAVER.
explanation.definitionFit: A semiquaver is the British name for a sixteenth note, half the length of a quaver, so a brief note in musical notation.

indicators.note: to broadcast is to scatter widely, as seed is cast, so the letters are scattered into new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A news bulletin cobbled together from bits and pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' reads as the verb a news programme naturally takes, but it is the instruction to rearrange the four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewn is the past participle of sew, meaning joined with needle and thread, exactly as stitched pieces are.

indicators.note: being outside something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps around another

blocks.note: a mister is a man, a chap
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A man standing outside a recently built church.
explanation.walkthrough: MISTER wraps around N.
explanation.definitionFit: A minster is a large or important church, often one that began as a monastery, such as York Minster.

blocks.note: first meaning: an academic award such as a master's degree
second meaning: a proviso or limiting condition attached to a statement

explanation.surface: Masters, perhaps golfers at the famous tournament, in good shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Masters' suggests the golf tournament or people in charge; 'say' flags it as an example of a degree.
explanation.definitionFit: A degree is an academic award earned by study, and a reservation limiting an agreement is also called this word.

clue.text: Poorly, brave OAP better than expected

indicators.note: something poorly is in bad shape, so these letters are knocked out of their order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An ill but courageous pensioner doing better than anyone expected.
explanation.walkthrough: An OAP is a British old-age pensioner; here the three letters simply join the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Par is the standard or expected level, from golf scores, so being over it means exceeding normal expectations.

clue.text: Live with team in cricket match after opener dismissed

indicators.note: the opener is whoever goes in first, so sending that one away removes the initial letter
being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: a cricket or football team has eleven players, XI in Roman numerals
a Test is an international cricket match; without its first letter it leaves these three

explanation.surface: Spending your life with a side playing a cricket match once the first batsman is out.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test match is international cricket. Drop its T, then put XI inside what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: To exist is to be alive or to have being, the same as to live in the intransitive sense.

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the letters run in the opposite direction

blocks.note: taken as written
an LP is a long-playing vinyl record

explanation.surface: An intention to record a backing track in the studio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' sounds like a backing track for the record, but it reverses TO plus LP.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot is a secret scheme or plan, and as a verb to plot is to plan a course of action.

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the closing letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: the final letter of medal
to earn something is to win it through effort

explanation.surface: At last a medal is won and collected from the podium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' looks like collecting the medal; it is the definition, in the sense of acquiring a skill.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick up a language or skill is to acquire knowledge of it, which is a common synonym for learning it.

indicators.note: cutting into something means going inside it, so one piece splits another apart

blocks.note: a tip is the end of something
taken as written
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A stylish hint from a hairdresser about cutting hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word, but it is part of the piece that goes inside; 'tip' is the end of something, not advice.
explanation.definitionFit: Trendiness is the quality of following current fashion, so the noun fashion, meaning modishness, matches it.

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
to do something promptly is to do it now

explanation.surface: Money and silver given back without delay.
explanation.walkthrough: Wonga is British slang for money. AG then NOW, read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Wonga is informal British slang for money, the same everyday sense as cash in hand.

clue.text: Speak about one with spirit in spring

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the others

blocks.note: to orate is to speak formally
I is the Roman numeral one
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: Talking about someone full of spirit in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' looks like the season; it is the verb, as in to spring from something.
explanation.definitionFit: To spring from a source is to arise or have its beginning there, the same meaning as originate.

clue.text: Old American dancer is dancing round Canada!

indicators.note: dancing letters move about the floor and land in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, then rearranged
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A veteran American dancer is touring all around Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' reads as a container signal, but it is part of the fodder; IS stays put and the other eleven letters dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Isadora Duncan was an early twentieth-century American performer regarded as a pioneer of modern dance.

blocks.note: surface reading: prepared to set off on a journey
setter's reading: a small child able to 'go' to the lavatory by themselves

explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' is a euphemism for using the lavatory, so readiness here is a toddler's milestone, not a departure.
explanation.definitionFit: A child who has learned to use the potty or lavatory unaided is ready to relieve themselves properly.

clue.text: Tantrums arising over card for players’ association

indicators.note: in a down answer, arising means reading upwards, so the letters go in reverse
in a down answer, over means placed above, so one piece comes before the next

blocks.note: a strop is a sulky fit of bad temper, British slang
a club is a playing card of the suit of clubs

explanation.surface: Players throwing fits over a card shown by a referee to a union of players.
explanation.walkthrough: A strop is a British word for a bad-tempered sulk; read it upwards and put the playing card below.
explanation.definitionFit: A sports club is an organisation whose members play games together, so it is a society of players.

indicators.note: someone distraught is upset and agitated, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: P is the abbreviation for power in physics
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A zealot in power while the empress is beside herself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container signal but just links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A partisan is a fervent, unquestioning supporter of a cause or party, much like a zealot or devotee.

clue.text: Capital on river east of Bristol, ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter of the word is used
in an across answer east is to the right, so the following pieces come after

blocks.note: the last letter of Bristol
taken as written
the Don is a river in Yorkshire, and another in Russia

explanation.surface: A capital city set on a river lying east of Bristol, which London is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On river' suggests the Thames, but river gives the Don; the L from Bristol comes first because the rest sits east of it.
explanation.definitionFit: London is the capital city of England and of the United Kingdom, the seat of government.

clue.text: Party whip upstanding given introduction of lady, dimpled little thing

indicators.note: in a down answer, standing up means reading from bottom to top, the opposite direction
an introduction comes at the start, so only the opening letter is used

blocks.note: Lab is short for the Labour Party
to flog is to whip
the first letter of lady

explanation.surface: A Party whip rising to meet a lady with dimples, a little sweetie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party whip' looks like one political official, but it splits in two, and both words are read upwards together; Lab is the British shorthand for the Labour Party.
explanation.definitionFit: The small white sphere used in golf has a surface covered in shallow dents that improve its flight.

indicators.note: some means a part of, so the answer is a portion of the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of one word, the next, and the start of the last

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry about a little perisher, a cheeky so-and-so.
explanation.walkthrough: Perisher is British slang for an annoying child; the answer straddles three words and ends inside the definition itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A scallywag is a mischievous, cheeky person, especially a child, which is just what a rascal is.

blocks.note: first meaning: a forward in football whose job is to score
second meaning: a worker who leaves the job in industrial action

explanation.surface: An assailant who is simply leaving the scene?
explanation.walkthrough: Walking out is the idiom for going on strike, not just leaving a room.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a forward player who scores goals and an employee who joins industrial action by withdrawing labour.

clue.text: Sticky food ladies stuck on second

indicators.note: something stuck on is attached at the end, so one piece follows the other

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, a second
lasses are girls or young women

explanation.surface: Ladies glued to something tacky they ate for a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: Mo is British informal for a moment, as in 'half a mo'.
explanation.definitionFit: Molasses is the thick dark syrup left after refining sugar, a gooey food ingredient used in baking.

indicators.note: a place toured by someone is travelled all round, so one piece is circled by another

blocks.note: CH is the international code for Switzerland
stellar and solar both mean relating to a star

explanation.surface: A brilliant student touring Switzerland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stellar' wants to mean outstanding, describing the student; it is the star sense, giving SOLAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar is a learned person or someone studying at school or university, especially one holding a scholarship.

blocks.note: going straight means not deviating
flush means level, even with a surface

explanation.surface: An instruction to run in a straight line, even.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' sounds like an athletic instruction; in poker a run is a sequence of consecutive cards.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker this hand is five consecutive cards all in one suit, so it is a sequence of ranks.

indicators.note: a heading sits at the top, so only the first letter of the word is used

blocks.note: a judge hears or tries a case in court
the first letter of town

explanation.surface: An attempt at making for the middle of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try' looks like attempt, but it is the courtroom sense of hearing a case.
explanation.definitionFit: The heart of a place is its central part, as in the heart of the city, so it is a synonym of centre.

indicators.note: shutting something in encloses it, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: cardinal is a deep scarlet colour
taken as written

explanation.surface: A churchman shut away in a private room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Study' looks like a room the cardinal is shut in, but it is the verb; the 's is 'has'. Cardinal here is the scarlet colour of a cardinal's robes.
explanation.definitionFit: To read a subject is to study it, especially at a British university, as in reading history.

clue.text: African water discovered in Angola, Kenya as amazing?

indicators.note: discovered means found lying inside, so a run of letters is taken from within the words that follow
to amaze once meant to bewilder or confuse, so these letters are muddled into a new order

blocks.note: a run of letters from the end of the first word through the last

explanation.surface: A wonderful stretch of water found in Angola and Kenya.
explanation.walkthrough: It looks like a plain hidden word, but the run of letters has the A and S the wrong way round at the end, so 'amazing' is needed to put them right.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Nyasa, also called Lake Malawi, is a large freshwater lake in the African Rift Valley.

blocks.note: surface reading: let something sink slightly further down
setter's reading: give birth to a young lower, one that moos, as a cow does

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower' is the noun for something that lows, i.e. moos, so a little lower is a baby cow; to drop young is to give birth.
explanation.definitionFit: When a cow gives birth it delivers a young animal of its kind, the farming verb for bovine birth.

indicators.note: something gripped is held tight inside, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
bro is short for brother

explanation.surface: A pen clutched by a family member.
explanation.walkthrough: A Biro is the British everyday name for a ballpoint pen; I goes inside BRO.
explanation.definitionFit: Biro is a trade name for a ballpoint pen that has become the general British word for one.

indicators.note: a drunken person staggers about, so the letters reel into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Drunken young men and a sailor getting into a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: A rating is a non-commissioned sailor, which makes the surface a brawl; here the word is just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalingrad was the long Second World War siege and clash in which Soviet forces defeated the German Sixth Army.
